task.name: Stories that land work within the reporting invocation are reported ALREADY_DONE, disowning the run that produced them
task.story_text:
## What happened

In sprint `issues-2030,2029,2129,1906,1880,1415,728,727` (run `675e2792fa1b`,
sprint `840e994353ba`), which began 2026-08-02 19:32 PT, `forge status` reported
five stories with status `done` and detail `ALREADY_DONE (merged)`:

| Story | Issue closed (PT) | Reported cost | Reported elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1880 | 19:51 | $3.82 | blank |
| #2129 | 20:04 | $6.46 | blank |
| #727  | 20:20 | $28.09 | blank |
| #728  | 20:53 | $11.93 | blank |
| #1906 | 21:04 | $2.39 | blank |

Every one of those issues was closed by a commit produced inside that same run,
between 19:51 and 21:04 PT — all after the sprint began at 19:32. Each carries a
non-zero cost for the run that is disowning the work.

A story genuinely skipped because its work was already merged performs no work
and costs nothing; #1906 records that shape as `outcome_source:
resume_skip_merged` with zero cost and zero time. These five ran dev and review
phases and landed commits.

The orchestrator serving this display is v0.13.0rc16 (tagged 2026-08-01 23:16
PT). Commit `a5645eb` — the fix for #2096, "Completed stories that landed a
commit are reported ALREADY_DONE, overwriting the DONE the coordinator recorded"
— is an ancestor of the `v0.13.0rc16` tag, so the fix for this symptom is
present in the running binary. Commit `01b3e47` (#1906) is not in rc16, and
concerns the opposite direction of the misreport.

## What was expected

A story whose work was performed and landed during the invocation that is
reporting should be attributed to that invocation. The bucket meaning
"completion was established before this run" describes how completion came
about, not merely that the branch is now merged; a story's own in-run landing
must not requalify it as pre-existing work, and the passage of time within a run
must not erode an outcome the coordinator already recorded.

However a story's disposition is reached, the reported outcome, cost, and
elapsed time should agree with one another. A story reported as having done
nothing in the current run should not simultaneously report a cost and a set of
executed phases for that run; where they disagree, the recorded execution is the
authoritative account of what happened.

## Diagnosis

> ⚠ Partial diagnosis — the investigation hit its budget or timeout before reaching a confirmed cause. Operator review required.

**Baseline:** `c3fad95337425577afd0c130fe9683a25a1807da` captured at `2026-08-03T05:53:57.597955+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/status_reader.py` — `sha256:23885b58998c59cdd05463d69692c0d4a85a84324e11633a5d0ac6feb0c42a1c`
- `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py` — `sha256:39768d816079d66635ecfd2e73141b4e7224a9a4f6a5ce35ef797dc95e61601b`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:b49ff97e9bc3fe8261a94dbe7e4eda1f91aebe67ed78c24030ef909a0e20d9d0`
- `src/theforge/sprint/dag.py` — `sha256:1b37c49866ff1f1856c126cf6a017c39d5b3c81a33803fd699f03f5675ce7df0`
- `src/theforge/sprint/story_state.py` — `sha256:bc0335aba24b3436cc1f5a82c01da5301cdef84c9ee642426c8a2c20c8c2c399`
- `.forge/sprints/840e994353ba/state.yaml` — `sha256:e1749216f5cebbd1b2421ed0bfe0ebac8ff50d02340d56732ddec26034e0e9f8`
- `.forge/logs/issues-2030,2029,2129,1906,1880,1415,728,727/run-675e2792fa1b.log` — `sha256:b7293648c42a1fd4357db0c4fb11e5ac3353e18952f330ffb3bf7beb379de029`

### Observed symptom

In sprint issues-2030,2029,2129,1906,1880,1415,728,727 (run 675e2792fa1b),
`forge status` / the persisted sprint state reported stories that had just
been developed, reviewed, and landed by *this same run* as
`ALREADY_DONE (merged)` with `outcome_source: resume_skip_merged` — the
classification meant for work a prior generation already finished. This
both misattributes the cost/effort away from the run that earned it and
(for #728) survives permanently in the on-disk accumulated sprint state
even after the run completes.

### Reproduction / evidence

Run log .forge/logs/issues-2030,2029,2129,1906,1880,1415,728,727/run-675e2792fa1b.log:
  - 20:51:46.078 [issue-728] "✓ DONE   total=$11.93  19m 5s" — issue-728
    finishes DEV+REVIEW normally in this run, cost measured, APPROVE.
  - 20:51:55.788 [sprint] "INFO issue-728: PR auto-merge queued; waiting
    for GitHub to report MERGED" — landing is asynchronous/in-flight.
  - 20:53:42.890 [issue-1415] "Source updated after pull — re-execing to
    load new code" — a mid-sprint, whole-process re-exec fires (source on
    the base branch changed under the running worker).
  - 20:54:58.692 [sprint] "issue-728            SKIP MERGED (already
    merged in PR #2146, skipping)" — the *new* process generation
    re-triages every story (reconcile=True is treated as resume-equivalent
    for re-exec too), and by now #728's queued PR has actually merged, so
    the git-only `_triage_spec` check reports `skip_merged`.
  - 20:56:51.485 [sprint] "SKIP issue-728 (already merged in PR #2146,
    skipping)" confirms it is never re-dispatched — it is simply relabeled.

Persisted evidence: .forge/sprints/840e994353ba/state.yaml (the accumulated
per-sprint story-state file written by persist_accumulated_story_state) —
issue-728's entry has outcome: ALREADY_DONE, outcome_source:
resume_skip_merged, story_run_id: 675e2792fa1b (this run's own id),
cost_usd: 11.9258, started_at/finished_at matching the DONE run above —
i.e. real cost/timestamps from this run's own completion were carried
forward, but the outcome itself was overwritten to ALREADY_DONE by the
post-re-exec triage. (Issues #1880, #2129, #727, #1906 in the same run show
outcome: DONE, outcome_source: null — they did not straddle a mid-sprint
re-exec boundary the way #728 did.)

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** The rc16 fix for #2096/#2042 (commit a5645eb) did not cover this case — it patched the re-exec *live-status* hardcoding for stories a prior generation already finished before this generation started, not the case of a story finishing *during* this generation with landing still in flight when re-exec fires.
  - Evidence: a5645eb touches only the REASON_RECONCILE_PRIOR_DONE path (runner.py ~4355-4366), which is a *different* branch from the skip_merged/triage path (~4390-4395, ~4260-4293) that this run actually hit. #728 never goes through REASON_RECONCILE_PRIOR_DONE — its drop_reason is unset; it hits the `_triage and _triage.action == "skip_merged"` branch instead, which a5645eb did not touch.
- **[ruled out]** `_triage_spec` (dag.py) itself is buggy — it should not report "merged" for a branch that just landed.
  - Evidence: `_triage_spec` is a pure git/audit-trail probe with no notion of "which sprint run produced this merge" — that is its whole design (it exists to detect genuinely pre-existing merged work across independent invocations). Its answer ("branch X is merged to base") is factually correct at the moment it runs. The defect is that callers treat "currently merged" and "was already merged before this generation started" as the same thing.
- **[confirmed]** The `if resume:`/live-state-init code that classifies a triage `skip_merged` result unconditionally builds ALREADY_DONE / resume_skip_merged detail without checking whether this exact story was already recorded DONE by an earlier generation of the very same sprint run (i.e. it doesn't distinguish "merged before this run started" from "merged by this run's own immediately-preceding process image, moments before a mid-run re-exec").
  - Evidence: runner.py `_already_done_story_entry` (~4260-4293) and the live-state initial-detail block (~4390-4395) both write `"outcome": "ALREADY_DONE", "outcome_source": "resume_skip_merged"` solely from `triage.action == "skip_merged"`. The former does reuse `prior_entry` (recovered_prior_entries_by_ref) for cost/timestamps/ verdict/story_run_id, which is why #728's entry carries this run's own real cost ($11.93) and timestamps — but it never checks `prior_entry.get("outcome")`, so a `prior_entry` that was itself already recorded DONE by the pre-re-exec generation gets its outcome field silently replaced with ALREADY_DONE anyway.

### Confirmed cause

When a mid-sprint whole-process re-exec occurs (triggered by a source
update pulled by a *different*, still-running story), the new process
generation's reconcile/resume path re-triages every story from scratch via
`_triage_spec`, which classifies purely on current git/PR merge state. For
a story that finished DEV+REVIEW and had its landing queued (async
auto-merge) in the generation that just exited, the merge frequently
completes in the gap before/around the re-exec. The new generation's
triage then sees "merged" and returns `skip_merged`, and both
`_already_done_story_entry` and the live-state initial-detail block
(src/theforge/sprint/runner.py) unconditionally stamp
`outcome: ALREADY_DONE` / `outcome_source: resume_skip_merged` for that
slug — without checking whether the recovered prior entry for the same
story already recorded a genuine, cost-bearing `DONE` from this same
sprint run's own preceding process image. The recovered entry's cost and
timestamps are carried forward (which is why the misreported row still
shows the real spend), but its `outcome` is discarded and replaced with
the resume-skip label, so the run that actually did and paid for the work
is reported as having done nothing.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:
  - `_already_done_story_entry` (~lines 4260-4293), used inside the
    `if resume:` accumulated-state persistence block (~4256-4331)
  - the live-state initial-story-detail construction for
    `_triage.action == "skip_merged"` (~lines 4390-4395)
Both consult `triages`/`triage.action` (built at ~3389-3412 via
`_triage_spec` in src/theforge/sprint/dag.py) without cross-checking
`recovered_prior_entries_by_ref[canonical_ref].get("outcome")` /
`.get("outcome_source")` before deciding the classification.

### Fix-success criterion

A story that a coordinator run has already recorded as `DONE` (with a
measured cost) for the current sprint must keep reporting `DONE` for that
same cost/story_run_id even when a mid-sprint re-exec re-triages it and
observes the branch as merged afterward — `outcome_source` must never be
set to `resume_skip_merged` for a slug whose recovered prior entry already
shows a non-ALREADY_DONE success outcome from the same sprint. Concretely:
re-running this exact scenario (dev/review completes, PR merge queued,
re-exec fires before the merge is confirmed) must leave `forge status` and
`.forge/sprints/<id>/state.yaml` showing `outcome: DONE`,
`outcome_source: null`, with the original cost/timestamps intact — not
`ALREADY_DONE`/`resume_skip_merged`.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- `_persist_current_story_result` records a story's `outcome` from `result.phase.name` rather than the fully-classified `StoryOutcome` produced by `_classify_and_record`, so the accumulated entry's outcome can momentarily diverge from the canonical structure's outcome before landing resolves (queued-PR window). Not the cause of this issue (the overwrite happens later, in the post-re-exec triage path), but a related fragility in the same accumulated-state bookkeeping area.

### Notes

I did not find the exact point where `recovered_prior_entries_by_ref`
fails to prevent the overwrite via `_resume_accumulated_by_ref.setdefault`
(that call *should* no-op when the key already exists with a DONE outcome)
— full confirmation of that specific mechanics would need a live repro
with instrumentation across the re-exec boundary, which was outside this
investigation's budget. The evidence is strong enough (real cost/timestamps
carried forward, outcome overwritten) that the fix belongs in
`_already_done_story_entry`/the live-state init block regardless of the
exact reason the `setdefault` guard doesn't hold in this path — that guard
itself may need to become an explicit outcome-aware merge rather than
key-presence-only.

handoff.summary: A mid-sprint whole-process re-exec re-triages every story purely from current git state, so a story that this run carried to DONE — with its auto-merge queued and completing around the re-exec boundary — was observed as `skip_merged` and unconditionally restamped `ALREADY_DONE`/`resume_skip_merged`, disowning the run that did and paid for the work while that same row still reported the cost and phases. I added `_recorded_prior_done(slug, canonical_ref)` to runner.py, which asks whether this sprint already recorded the story as run-to-DONE (canonical `_story_state`, seeded from the accumulated file, or the recovered accumulated entry), and `_skip_merged_outcome(slug, canonical_ref)`, which returns `(DONE, None)` in that case and the previous `(ALREADY_DONE, 'resume_skip_merged')` otherwise. It is applied at all three skip_merged classification sites: the `if reconcile:` persist block (the one that produced the #728 state.yaml row), `_already_done_story_entry` in the resume persist block, and the live-status initial-detail block that `forge status` renders. The existing `_reconciled_prior_outcome` (a5645eb's fix for #2096/#2042) now delegates to the shared `_recorded_prior_done` so both directions of the misreport obey one rule.

The converse is pinned by test_reexec_skip_merged_preserves_prior_already_done_as_noop, which keeps ALREADY_DONE/resume_skip_merged for a genuine prior no-op.

story_deviations: Modified one assertion in an existing test: tests/test_sprint_resume.py::test_reexec_summary_preserves_prior_story_accounting_from_progressive_state asserted `outcome_source == 'resume_skip_merged'` for a prior-DONE $3.50 story hit by a skip_merged re-exec triage — the exact shape this story defines as the defect. It now asserts `outcome == 'DONE'` and `outcome_source is None`, with a comment citing #2150. The rest of that test (cost, started_at/finished_at, sprint duration) is unchanged; that is its stated purpose.
deferred_items: Out of scope per spec: `_persist_current_story_result` records outcome from `result.phase.name` rather than the classified StoryOutcome (related fragility in the same bookkeeping area, not the cause here).

The Notes' suggestion that `_resume_accumulated_by_ref.setdefault` become an outcome-aware merge was not needed: it is seeded from `recovered_prior_entries_by_ref`, so it already no-ops when a prior entry exists. With `_already_done_story_entry` now outcome-aware, both branches agree. A prior *non-succeeded* entry (e.g. FAILED) whose branch reads as merged still keeps its FAILED entry — pre-existing behaviour, untouched.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
